subject: ARA
label: Grade 03
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 03 Arabic, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 4 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Reading simple passages
modules.outcome: read and answer questions on a short text
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Reading simple passages', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: read and answer questions on a short text. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Reading simple passages' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: read and answer questions on a short text, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: الولد يلعب في الحديقة. أين يلعب الولد؟ في الحديقة. (The boy plays in the garden. Where does the boy play? In the garden.) Method: Model run for 'Reading simple passages'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Read and answer questions on a short text: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Read this short passage I wrote. أَنَا أُحِبُّ الْمَدْرَسَةَ. فِي صَفِّي عِشْرُونَ طَالِبًا. مُعَلِّمَتِي تَقْرَأُ لَنَا قِصَّةً كُلَّ يَوْمٍ. [I love school. In my class there are twenty students. My teacher reads us a story every day.] Read it twice, then underline the numbers.

Step 2, Find the key words. الْمَدْرَسَةُ [school], صَفٌّ [class], طَالِبٌ [student], قِصَّةٌ [story], كُلَّ يَوْمٍ [every day]. Say what each sentence is about before answering. The first is about liking school, the second about the class, the third about the story.

Step 3, Answer questions with a full sentence. كَمْ طَالِبًا فِي الصَّفِّ؟ [How many students are in the class?] فِي الصَّفِّ عِشْرُونَ طَالِبًا. [In the class there are twenty students.] مَاذَا تَقْرَأُ الْمُعَلِّمَةُ؟ [What does the teacher read?] تَقْرَأُ قِصَّةً. [She reads a story.]

Step 4, Ask a when-question. مَتَى تَقْرَأُ الْمُعَلِّمَةُ الْقِصَّةَ؟ [When does the teacher read the story?] تَقْرَأُهَا كُلَّ يَوْمٍ. [She reads it every day.] Notice how the answer repeats words from the text, which proves you found it in the passage.

Step 5, Fix an error. A student answers the question كَمْ طَالِبًا فِي الصَّفِّ؟ with the single word كَثِيرٌ [many]. Correction: go back to the text; the number is عِشْرُونَ, so the full answer is عِشْرُونَ طَالِبًا. Guessing is not reading.

Step 6, Your turn: answer who reads us a story and where is the class. Model answer: مُعَلِّمَتِي تَقْرَأُ لَنَا قِصَّةً. [My teacher reads us a story.] صَفِّي فِي الْمَدْرَسَةِ. [My class is at school.] Check you copied the spelling.

modules.title: Nouns and verbs
modules.outcome: tell nouns from verbs and use them in sentences
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Nouns and verbs', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: tell nouns from verbs and use them in sentences. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Nouns and verbs' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: tell nouns from verbs and use them in sentences, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: In 'Mira has a dog called Bruno', 'dog' is a common noun, 'Mira' and 'Bruno' are proper nouns and need capital letters. Method: Model run for 'Nouns and verbs'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Tell nouns from verbs and use them in sentences: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Know what a noun is. الِاسْمُ [the noun] names a person, thing or place: وَلَدٌ [boy], كِتَابٌ [book], مَدْرَسَةٌ [school]. A quick test: you can put الْ before a noun, as in الْكِتَابُ [the book]. Collect five nouns from your bag.

Step 2, Know what a verb is. الْفِعْلُ [the verb] shows an action. Past: كَتَبَ [he wrote], ذَهَبَ [he went], جَلَسَ [he sat]. Present: يَكْتُبُ [he writes], يَذْهَبُ [he goes], يَجْلِسُ [he sits]. You cannot say الْ before a verb.

Step 3, Put them together. الْوَلَدُ يَقْرَأُ الْكِتَابَ. [The boy reads the book.] ذَهَبَتِ الْبِنْتُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ. [The girl went to school.] In the first sentence الْوَلَدُ and الْكِتَابَ are nouns and يَقْرَأُ is the verb.

Step 4, Sort a list. قَلَمٌ، يَرْسُمُ، بِنْتٌ، أَكَلَ، شَجَرَةٌ. [pen, he draws, girl, he ate, tree] Nouns: قَلَمٌ، بِنْتٌ، شَجَرَةٌ. Verbs: يَرْسُمُ، أَكَلَ. Each noun can take الْ; the verbs cannot.

Step 5, Fix an error. A child labels يَلْعَبُ [he plays] as a noun. Correction: it is a verb, because it shows an action and الْيَلْعَبُ is impossible. Another error is calling كُرَةٌ [ball] a verb; كُرَةٌ names a thing, so it is a noun.

Step 6, Your turn: write a sentence with the noun بِنْتٌ and the verb تَرْسُمُ [she draws], then name noun and verb. Model answer: الْبِنْتُ تَرْسُمُ شَجَرَةً. [The girl draws a tree.] Nouns: الْبِنْتُ، شَجَرَةً. Verb: تَرْسُمُ.

modules.title: Daily life and the beach
modules.outcome: describe a day and a trip
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Daily life and the beach', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: describe a day and a trip. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Daily life and the beach' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: describe a day and a trip, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: في الصيف الجو حار وفي الشتاء الجو بارد. أذهب إلى الشاطئ في الصيف. (In summer it is hot, in winter cold. I go to the beach in summer.) Method: Model run for 'Daily life and the beach'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Describe a day and a trip: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Describe your morning in the present. أَسْتَيْقِظُ فِي السَّاعَةِ السَّابِعَةِ. [I wake up at seven o'clock.] أَغْسِلُ وَجْهِي. [I wash my face.] أَتَنَاوَلُ الْفُطُورَ. [I have breakfast.] أَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ. [I go to school.] Say them in order.

Step 2, Describe the rest of the day. أَعُودُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ. [I return home.] أَكْتُبُ وَاجِبِي. [I do my homework.] أَلْعَبُ مَعَ أَخِي. [I play with my brother.] أَنَامُ فِي السَّاعَةِ التَّاسِعَةِ. [I sleep at nine o'clock.]

Step 3, Describe a trip to the beach in the past. ذَهَبْنَا إِلَى الشَّاطِئِ. [We went to the beach.] لَعِبْتُ بِالرَّمْلِ. [I played with the sand.] سَبَحَ أَخِي فِي الْبَحْرِ. [My brother swam in the sea.] كَانَ الْجَوُّ جَمِيلًا. [The weather was beautiful.]

Step 4, Compare present and past. الْيَوْمَ أَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ. [Today I go to school.] أَمْسِ ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى الشَّاطِئِ. [Yesterday I went to the beach.] The present verb begins with أَ for I; the past verb ends with تُ for I.

Step 5, Fix an error. A child says أَمْسِ أَذْهَبُ إِلَى الشَّاطِئِ. Correction: أَمْسِ [yesterday] needs the past, so say أَمْسِ ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى الشَّاطِئِ. Match the time word with the right verb form every time.

Step 6, Your turn: write about your morning and yesterday's trip, one sentence each. Model answer: أَسْتَيْقِظُ مُبَكِّرًا وَأَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ. أَمْسِ ذَهَبْنَا إِلَى الشَّاطِئِ وَلَعِبْتُ بِالرَّمْلِ. [I wake up early and go to school. Yesterday we went to the beach and I played in the sand.]

modules.title: Writing short sentences
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Writing short sentences', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: write three connected sentences. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Writing short sentences' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: write three connected sentences, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: هذا كتاب. هذه قطة. أنا أحب مدرستي. (This is a book. This is a cat. I love my school.) Method: Model run for 'Writing short sentences'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Write three connected sentences: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, A good short text has three connected sentences: what, then what, and why or how I felt. Plan before you write. Topic: a visit to the park. Sentence one says where, sentence two says what you did, sentence three says how you felt.
Step 2, Write sentence one. ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى الْحَدِيقَةِ مَعَ أُسْرَتِي. [I went to the park with my family.] Begin with a clear verb and add a place. Put a full stop at the end of the sentence.

Step 3, Write sentence two with a linking word. ثُمَّ لَعِبْتُ مَعَ صَدِيقِي بِالْكُرَةِ. [Then I played with my friend with the ball.] ثُمَّ means then. Other linking words are وَ [and] and بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ [after that].

Step 4, Write sentence three with a reason. كُنْتُ سَعِيدًا لِأَنَّ الْجَوَّ كَانَ جَمِيلًا. [I was happy because the weather was beautiful.] لِأَنَّ means because. Now read all three together: ذَهَبْتُ... ثُمَّ... كُنْتُ سَعِيدًا...

Step 5, Fix an error. A child writes ذَهَبْتُ الْحَدِيقَةِ لَعِبْتُ سَعِيدًا. Correction: add إِلَى [to], a linking word and a reason, so the text reads clearly: ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى الْحَدِيقَةِ. ثُمَّ لَعِبْتُ. كُنْتُ سَعِيدًا لِأَنَّ الْجَوَّ جَمِيلٌ.

Step 6, Your turn: write three connected sentences about a trip to the market. Model answer: ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى السُّوقِ مَعَ أُمِّي. ثُمَّ اشْتَرَيْنَا الْفَاكِهَةَ. كُنْتُ سَعِيدًا لِأَنِّي أُحِبُّ التُّفَّاحَ. [I went to the market with my mother. Then we bought fruit. I was happy because I love apples.]

Which action verb starts the outcome of Unit 1 (Reading simple passages), and at which Bloom level is it?
'read', at the Remember level. (Covered in unit 1: Reading simple passages.)
When do the formative checks FA1 to FA4 and the summative checks SA1 and SA2 happen?
FA1 to FA4 around weeks 6, 12, 24 and 30; SA1 in week 18; SA2 in week 36. (Covered in: Assessment plan, near the top of this page.)
In which weeks does Unit 4 (Writing short sentences) run?
Weeks 28 to 36. (Covered in unit 4: Writing short sentences.)
What evidence do you keep for each unit, and why?
One page in your learning book. It shows what you can really do and lets a teacher check it against the standard. (Covered in: How you are checked, further down this page.)
ladder: L1: say and read familiar words and short sentences.
L2: read short texts and write connected sentences.
L3: write paragraphs and speak on a topic with notes.
L4: write for different purposes and analyse how texts persuade.
L5: write and argue at length; handle unseen texts.
L6 (degree): academic reading, writing and citation.
L7 (postgraduate): publish, teach or translate with expert accuracy.
